opinion.hook: Tricky's 1995 cover of Public Enemy's 'Black Steel' offers a dark, raw reinterpretation.
opinion.summary: Martina Topley-Bird's vocals replace Chuck D's authority, creating an unsettling atmosphere. The production features abrasive sounds and fractured rhythms, building a sense of chaos. This version avoids reassurance, presenting pushback as confusion and menace. The track's fade-out acts as a countdown to a mental explosion.

opinion.headline: AI won’t create India’s jobs crisis, but it could deepen it
opinion.hook: Educated youth face a challenging job market with fewer middle-skill opportunities.
opinion.summary: Many new jobs are in low-productivity agriculture or informal services. AI threatens cognitive jobs, widening the existing skills divide. India must create productive non-farm work and expand tech-complementary roles. Targeted AI skilling is crucial to secure the demographic dividend.

opinion.headline: Public education needs public money
opinion.hook: Students across the nation have taken to the streets, drawing attention to the overwhelming resource deficit in education.
opinion.summary: With public funding stagnating and not meeting government commitments, many students are now gravitating towards private schools. This shift in enrollment is leading to the closure or merging of numerous government institutions. To enhance the quality of state schools and foster future development, a significant increase in public investment is imperative.

opinion.headline: This hotspot is getting hazardous
opinion.hook: Global humid heat exposure has surged significantly, with India experiencing a nineteenfold increase.
opinion.summary: Poor urban planning and construction have intensified heat traps in Indian cities. This humid heat stress poses serious health risks, impacting vital organs and vulnerable populations. Productivity losses have risen dramatically, affecting workdays and wages for many. Addressing humid heat stress requires urgent policy and political prioritization for human health.

opinion.headline: GS, the ultimate tech frontier to tap into
opinion.hook: Genuine stupidity is presented as a revolutionary technology surpassing artificial intelligence.
opinion.summary: This concept requires no advanced infrastructure, relying solely on human ingenuity. Corporations and governments will embrace this trend, announcing strategic pivots and unrealistic promises. Investors will support startups focused on this concept, with delivery being secondary. Universities and consultants will also adapt, offering new degrees and explanations for its adoption.

opinion.headline: Tech mastery and magic
opinion.hook: Mystery can evoke fear or excitement depending on individual attitudes and dispositions.
opinion.summary: Adam Waytz notes our era offers immense explainability and information access. Generative AI further expands this readily available knowledge base for everyone. However, this information overload risks leading to disenchantment and a loss of wonder. Embracing mystery can help regain intellectual humility and foster mutual understanding.
